tested_scope.question: Does a concrete zero-cost repository/target-native read path expose a monotonic minimum-generation witness after immutable release deletion and repository delete/recreate, without a mutating probe, protected/admin setup as an outcome dependency, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or external coordinator?

public_sources_checked.title: Immutable releases - GitHub Docs
observations: After an immutable release is deleted, its tag can be deleted but the same tag name cannot be reused.
The tag-name non-reuse protection survives repository deletion and recreation with the same repository name.
Publishing an immutable release automatically generates a release attestation.

public_sources_checked.title: REST API endpoints for releases - GitHub Docs
observations: The documented read surface lists published releases and can retrieve a published release by tag name.
The bounded documentation read did not expose a read endpoint for historical deleted immutable-release tag-name reservations or a monotonic minimum-generation tombstone.

public_sources_checked.title: Managing the lifecycle of artifact attestations - GitHub Docs
observations: After deletion, GitHub documents that the attestation can no longer be found on GitHub.

public_sources_checked.title: REST API endpoints for artifact attestations - GitHub Docs
observations: Attestations can be listed by subject digest subject to repository ownership/read permissions.
The bounded documentation read did not establish an undeletable cross-repository-resurrection minimum-generation floor.

factors: stale transition kind = same historical tag replay or previously-unused lower-generation tag
synthetic_model.model_note: For repository delete/recreate, undocumented cross-resurrection visibility of old attestation/release records is treated as unavailable rather than assumed. This is a fail-closed acceptance assumption, not evidence that GitHub necessarily deletes every underlying record.

result.new_positive_evidence: GitHub's immutable-release service-side tag-name non-reuse remains a strong duplicate-replay fence for a previously used stable tag name, including repository resurrection.
result.new_falsification: The bounded documented read surfaces do not provide a concrete read-visible monotonic minimum-generation floor after deletion. Current release reads lose the deleted release object, artifact attestations are themselves deletable and then unfindable, and tag-name anti-reuse is only an oracle for previously used names and becomes observable through a write attempt rather than a pure read. It also cannot reject a previously-unused stale lower-generation tag.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A target/repository-native non-mutating read endpoint or sink-side rule that exposes/enforces a monotonic minimum generation across release deletion and repository delete/recreate, and cannot itself be rolled back, deleted, hidden or bypassed by a previously-unused stale transition identifier.
result.scope_guard: This result is limited to the documented GitHub surfaces and the 64-scenario abstract model above. It does not prove absence of an undocumented internal tombstone, does not generalize to arbitrary sinks, and does not treat mutating anti-reuse probes or admin configuration as accepted outcome dependencies.

observed: GitHub documents immutable-release tag-name non-reuse after release deletion and repository resurrection.
GitHub documents artifact-attestation deletion and subsequent unfindability.
GitHub release read APIs are documented around existing published release objects.
inferred: Without a documented read-visible historical reservation/floor, a stateless read-only worker cannot use the anti-reuse tombstone as a minimum-generation witness.
A write-probe anti-reuse oracle is insufficient for the accepted route because it is mutating and still fails previously-unused lower-generation identifiers.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_rate_limit_dependency: Lightweight reads remain rate-limited transport and must checkpoint/return rather than use API volume as compute.

continuation: Part99: execute exactly one bounded read-only indistinguishability leaf for the hidden immutable-tag reservation state. Construct two histories that have identical current documented read surfaces: A = candidate tag name was never used; B = same tag name backed an immutable release and both release/tag were later deleted. Verify whether any public read-only GitHub endpoint can distinguish A from B without creating/updating a ref/release, requiring protected/admin setup as an outcome dependency, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or an external coordinator. If no endpoint exists, formalize that tag-name anti-reuse is a service-side write-time duplicate fence but not a stateless read-visible freshness floor, and preserve sink-side minimum-generation enforcement as the unresolved alternative child.
